title: Learner Drivers: Licence, Supervisor & L Plates
whatItIs: A learner needs a provisional licence (apply from 15 years 9 months), a qualified supervisor and L plates. Only an ADI can take a learner on a motorway.

keyFacts.text: Learners MUST hold a valid provisional licence and pass the practical test before driving unaccompanied.
The supervisor MUST be 21+ and have held a full licence for that type of car (manual or automatic) for 3 years.
Red L plates MUST be clearly visible from the front and the back. In Wales, D plates can be used.
Learners MUST NOT use a motorway unless with an ADI, in a car with dual controls and L (or D) plates.
A supervisor MUST NOT use a hand-held phone while supervising.

items.label: Full licence held by the supervisor
Maximum fine for no proper supervision

a.label: Unpaid supervisor (family, friends)
points: Over 21, full licence for that type of car held 3 years
Cannot take the learner on a motorway

b.label: Paid teacher
points: Must be an ADI (green badge) or a trainee (pink badge)
Only an ADI, in a dual-control car, can take a learner on a motorway

onTheTest.question: A pupil's relative wants to supervise private practice in the pupil's manual car. Who meets the legal requirements?
options: Aged 24, full manual car licence held for 4 years
Aged 20, full manual car licence held for 3 years
Aged 30, full manual car licence held for 2 years
Aged 45, full automatic-only licence held for 20 years
onTheTest.why: The supervisor must be at least 21 and have held a full licence for that type of car (manual or automatic) for 3 years.

onTheTest.question: A provisional car licence holder wants motorway experience in Great Britain. When is this allowed?
options: With any supervisor who has held a full licence for 3 years
Only once they have passed the theory test
With an ADI, in a car with dual controls and L plates
Never, until they pass the practical driving test
onTheTest.why: Rule 253: provisional car licence holders must not use a motorway unless with an ADI in a dual-control car with L plates.

traps: Learners in Great Britain have the same speed limits as after the test and can drive day or night.
There is no minimum number of lessons or hours of practice.
No proper supervision: fine up to £1,000 and up to 6 points.
A provisional car licence holder must not drive while towing a trailer.
